title: Refuse session bind to a lane that does not exist
action: In packages/bee-rs/crates/bee/src/verbs/state_group/sessions.rs run_session_bind: after require_id resolves the lane and BEFORE acquire_sessions_lock, read the lane record (read_lane_strict) and return Out::Thrown(lane_missing_refusal("session bind", &lane)) when it is absent, so the bind is a zero-mutation refusal that never takes the lock. Add a unit test in verbs/state_group/tests.rs asserting bind to an unknown lane refuses and writes no lane key, and bind to a started lane still succeeds.
goal: A session can no longer enter the state the lane guard refuses on: bind fails closed at the moment the bad lane is named, with the FIX text naming state start-feature --as-lane.

truths: bind to a lane with no .bee/lanes/<f>.json refuses and the session record keeps no lane key
bind to a lane started with state start-feature --as-lane still succeeds
the refusal reuses lane_missing_refusal so its FIX names state start-feature --feature <f> --as-lane
prohibitions: No lock taken on the refusal path

trace.outcome: session bind refuses a lane with no .bee/lanes record, before the sessions lock, reusing the shared LANE_MISSING wording
trace.inline_reason: A dispatched worker inherits the orchestrator's cwd (decision 2026-08-12), which is the MAIN checkout — the worktree-first guard refuses source edits there, so the worker could not touch this feature's files. The orchestrator entered the worktree itself and ran the cell inline.
